'''Petr William Cornelie'''<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-31 |title=Avec Sekou Doumbouya, Monaco remporte son premier match de préparation |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/monaco-remporte-son-premier-match-de-preparation-face-a-bahcesehir/ |access-date=2023-08-31 |website=BeBasket |language=fr}}</ref> (born July 26, 1995) is a French-Czech professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Esenler Erokspor (basketball)|Esenler Erokspor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He stands 210 cm (6'11'’) tall and plays at both the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]] positions. Cornelie was selected by the [[Denver Nuggets]] with the 53rd pick of the [[2016 NBA draft]].

== Early life and career ==
Growing up in [[Alsace]], Cornelie played in the youth ranks of Saint-Joseph Strasbourg, Basket Club Souffelweyersheim and Association sportive d'Electricité de Strasbourg.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dna.fr/sports/2015/06/01/cornelie-l-alsacien|title=Cornelie, l'Alsacien|work=DNA.fr|date=June 1, 2015|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Le Mans Sarthe (2013–2019) ===
At the age of 15, Cornelie joined the youth academy of [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.letelegramme.fr/omnisports/cornelie-la-nouvelle-pepite-du-mans-06-09-2015-10763652.php|title=Cornelie, la nouvelle pépite du Mans|work=Le Telegramme|date=September 6, 2015|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> He made his debut on Le Mans' men's team during the 2013–14 season and became a regular on the team the following season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200006/Joueurs/A55324/Cornelie-Petr|title=Petr Cornelie – Le Mans – Joueurs – Pro A – LNB.fr|work=LNB.fr|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> In the 2014–15 season he won the Pro A Rising Star award.

On June 13, 2016, Cornelie was one of 13 different international underclassmen (including one of four other Frenchmen) to enter their names for the [[2016 NBA draft]]. Cornelie was eventually picked by the [[Denver Nuggets]] 53rd pick<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-select-murray-hernangomez-beasley-2016-nba-draft|title=Denver Nuggets Select Murray, Hernangomez and Beasley in First Round of 2016 NBA Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2016|accessdate=October 13, 2016}}</ref> and joined them for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-announce-2016-nba-summer-league-roster-and-minicamp-schedule-070116/|title=Nuggets Announce 2016 NBA Summer League Roster and Mini-Camp Schedule|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2016|accessdate=July 15, 2016}}</ref> He remained at Le Mans for the 2016–17 campaign. After a disappointing season, in which he averaged 4.1 points and 2.9 rebounds a game for Le Mans, Cornelie joined another Pro A club, the [[Levallois Metropolitans]], on loan in June 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Petr-cornelie-prete-par-le-mans-a-levallois/813946|title=Petr Cornélie prêté par Le Mans à Levallois|last=Rédaction|work=L'ÉQUIPE|access-date=2017-07-18|language=fr-FR}}</ref>

=== Pau-Orthez (2019–2021) ===
On June 20, 2019, Cornelie signed a deal with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/petr-cornelie-signs-with-pau-orthez/|title=Petr Cornelie signs with Pau-Orthez|date=June 20, 2019|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 25, 2019|archive-date=November 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211118171757/https://sportando.basketball/en/petr-cornelie-signs-with-pau-orthez/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2021–2022)===
On September 17, 2021, Cornelie signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Denver Nuggets]]. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Nuggets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets Sign Petr Cornelie to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-petr-cornelie-091721|website=NBA.com|date=September 17, 2021|access-date=September 18, 2021}}</ref> On January 9, 2022, he was waived by the Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Davon Reed to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-davon-reed-010922|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

===Grand Rapids Gold (2022)===
On January 15, 2022, Cornelie was acquired via returning player rights by the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 15, 2022|access-date=January 15, 2022}}</ref>

===Real Madrid (2022–2023)===
On July 27, 2022, Cornelie returned to Europe, signing a one-year contract with [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Petr Cornelie is a new Real Madrid player
|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/07/27/petr-cornelie-is-a-new-real-madrid-player|access-date=July 27, 2022|website=Realmadrid.com}}</ref> On June 26, 2023, he parted ways with the Spanish club.

===AS Monaco (2023–2025)===
[[File:Petr Cornelie 12 AS Monaco Basket EuroLeague 20241212 (3).jpg|thumb|right|Cornelie with [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]] in 2024]]
On July 19, 2023, Cornelie signed a three-year deal with French champions [[AS Monaco Basket|AS Monaco]].

===Esenler Erokspor (2025–present)===
On July 27, 2025, he signed with [[Esenler Erokspor (basketball)|Esenler Erokspor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite Instagram |user=esenlereroksporbasketbol |postid=DMupywINiLF|title=Petr Cornelie Esenler Erokspor’da! |date=July 27, 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Cornelie played for France at the 2012 U17 World Championships in Lithuania,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kaunas2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/fu17wc/men/player/p/eid/6228/pid/93515/rid//sid/6228/tid/282/profile.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801094955/http://kaunas2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/fu17wc/men/player/p/eid/6228/pid/93515/rid//sid/6228/tid/282/profile.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 1, 2012|title=Petr Cornelie profile, FIBA U17 World Championship for Men 2012|work=FIBA.COM|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> at the 2013 U18 European Championships in Latvia<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2013.roundID_9420.teamID_282.playerID_93515.html|title=Petr Cornelie {{!}} U18 European Championship Men (2013)|work=FIBAEurope.com|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> and at the 2015 U20 European Championships in Italy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/93515/sid/11585/tid/282/_/2015_U20_European_Championship_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151214034418/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/93515/sid/11585/tid/282/_/2015_U20_European_Championship_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 14, 2015|title=Petr Cornelie profile, U20 European Championship Men 2015|work=FIBA.COM|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His mother, Pavla Sigmundova, is a former Czech basketball player and his father, Martial Cornelie, played basketball in the Pro B, the second-tier of French basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Accueil/100003/Article/25656/Petr-Cornelie-le-futur-en-grand|title=Petr Cornelie, le futur en grand|work=LNB.fr|date=March 31, 2015|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> Petr's sister, Jodie Cornelie-Sigmundova, played internationally for the French junior national teams and spent four years on the University of Dayton Flyers women's basketball team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://daytonflyers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2498|title=Jodie Cornelie-Sigmundova – 2015–16 Women's Basketball|work=DaytonFlyers.com|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref>
